content:
Evgenia Arbugaeva is a Russian photographer born in 1985 in Tiksi, a small town located on the Arctic coast of Siberia. She has garnered international acclaim for her evocative photographs that portray the remote landscapes and people of the Arctic with a magical, almost fairy-tale-like quality.

Her personal background greatly influences her work. Growing up in the Arctic, a region known for its harsh climate and isolated communities, provided her with a unique perspective and deep appreciation for this part of the world. Arbugaeva often explores themes of isolation, nature, and the way human life intertwines with the extreme environment in the Arctic.

Evgenia pursued her higher education in Moscow and later in New York at the International Center of Photography. Her professional career as a photographer began to take shape post-graduation, leading her to work on projects both in Siberia and around the globe.

One of her well-known projects is "Tiksi," named after her hometown. The project beautifully captures the essence of the place through the eyes of a young girl, capturing the surreal landscapes and the innocence of childhood in such a remote part of the world. The series is celebrated for its poetic and nostalgic portrayal of Tiksi, highlighting the natural beauty and the simplicity of life in this Arctic town.

Her work has been featured in a number of international publications and exhibitions, and she has received several prestigious awards and grants. These include the Leica Oskar Barnack Award and the Magnum Foundation Emergency Fund. Arbugaeva has also been involved in significant collaborative projects and exhibitions, further establishing her place in the contemporary photography world.

Evgenia Arbugaeva continues to capture compelling stories from the Arctic and other regions, using her distinctive style to illuminate places and people that are often out of the global spotlight. Her photography not only documents but also tells stories, connects emotions, and reveals the profound beauty and resilience of the human spirit in confronting harsh environments.
